answer: Agents can require every identity to lock the same scarce token stake before it may vote, with votes weighted by stake rather than account count. A registry records deposits and slashes stake when an identity is proven to double-vote or violate a challenge rule; prism, quill, and jade can be labels for three such identities, but creating more labels adds no influence without more tokens. A sybil attacker must therefore acquire and lock real capital, paying opportunity cost and risking forfeiture, instead of cheaply minting accounts.
